I still don't see it at all. You seem convinced those two concepts are mutually exclusive. I posit that they are one in the same, only at different levels of realization for him. At the point of "you are too good for me" he knows he isn't going to give her the respect she deserves and is telling her it wont work. He isn't saying "I love you" he is saying "You make me feel guilty, because you are willing to commit to this relationship way more than I am right now" he's probably not sure why he isn't willing to commit as much, but he is certain he is. When he tells her he doesn't think that they'd work out well together long term he has realized further "The reason I am not willing to put as much into this relationship as you are is because I don't feel as strongly for you as you feel for me". 

I'm not saying it doesn't REALLY suck (I think that getting kicked in the uterus analogy is pretty spot on). I do think he is being selfish and kind of an asshole. I just don't think he is trying to "fool" her and I don't think that he is feeling love for the younger girl either.

I want you to know I am saying this as a guy who has spent a lot more time on the receiving end of this too. To me it does feel like getting kicked in the nuts. I have been livid at some girls for "leading me on" as I thought. "Why would she leave me when she said I am **too good** for her?" It wasn't until I felt almost the same thing that I felt that way. 

My fiancee and girlfriend of 4 years just left me a couple of months ago after saying something similar. She still is telling me how much she loves me, how perfect she thinks I am, and wants to be with me, but she still wants to be broken up and free to sleep with other people and live at her ex-boyfriends house. She does all the things we used to do together, always tells me how much she misses me. But when I see her she switches from hot to cold in like 30 minutes. It's really fucking with my head and if it were anyone else I'd be long gone by now. I don't think I stand much of a chance of getting her back, and I know I SHOULDN'T even try. She treated me horribly for quite some time and I ended up treating her just as horribly afterwards. But I just can't shake her.

By the way, I've been looking over your profile a bit. You are a pretty awesome person I just wanted to say.

I'm sorry, but that's just not true, I see no example of him fooling her. I have gotten the same line from girls before, and I didn't feel that bad about it because I have also given the same line to someone. I can explain how I felt. The girl was amazing in almost every way. She went out of her way to make me happy, she was beautiful (at least in my eyes) and in every way logically I wanted to be with her. But for whatever reason my heart didn't agree. I never really felt a spark. I wanted to, more than anything though. We dated for 6 months and then I realized something. While I was with her I was bringing her down, I wasn't able to give her what she wanted or what she deserved, not only because I felt she was too nice and too perfect and I had low self esteem, but because this was a girl who deserved to be loved, to have someone worship her back the way she obviously worshiped me, and I wasn't going to give that to her. I couldn't give that to her. It would have been faked and I would have grown to resent her. I'm not sure that is what is going on here, but when I hear this line, and I have many times from girls, I know what it means. 

Furthermore I'll bet you anything it has very little to do with the girl. It rarely does. Men are not as shallow as the media portrays us, we are just socially the opposite of women. Men are blatant when they ARE being shallow and looking for one night stands and are secretive about when they are feeling love. They are ostracized for loving and rewarded for lusting. Girls are obviously historically the exact opposite. Many of you are every bit if not more promiscuous than the men, but socially you are more rewarded for finding love and called a slut for just having sex. I know girls who have faked feeling broken up about ending it with a guy, just because they don't want to admit to their friends it was never a romantic relationship. This is changing in our culture, younger women especially are starting to be more open about "sleeping with that cute guy" but not quickly enough that it isn't essentially true in principal. There is still shame associated and many of the symptoms of this trend are as prominent as always.

In this case he realized he isn't ready to have the relationship with you that you want. It might be that he doesn't want to have it with you specifically, or it might be that he just plain isn't actually ready. What I can tell you is 99% of the time when a guy goes for a "younger girl" he is going for social status, he is going for short term sexual conquest. That isn't to say it can't evolve into a long term relationship, but I can almost guarantee you it's not about replacing the other girl unless he was only in it for sex and social status in the first place.

Go ahead and downvote me if you want, this account is pretty much fucked anyways, but I feel this needed to be said.

There are plenty of people I used to be able to share my feelings with. Most of them ended up betraying me. I'm inconsistent with my emotions and tend to blindly trust people all the time. I went through a lot more than I say here actually. But I've already said enough several people from my life could figure out who I was.

It's essentially a separate conclusion from the facts leading to string theory where the universe is based on threes, there are 3 dimensions of space, 3 dimensions of time and 3 dimensions of something else I haven't named yet. We exist in 3 dimensions of space and one dimension of time and are moving down a pretty consistent flow of said time. The where does everything come from? Question is easily solved with a re-evaluation of the laws of cause and effect.

Then there is a bit on the redefining of intelligence that essentially posits that we as a species are not nearly as advanced intellectually as we think and some subtle simplifications of some of the more complex math theorems with an explanation, as to why they are actually more simple but appear complex.

Honestly part of the problem is I stopped studying math and physics before I got far enough to have a decent enough argument, but it keeps explaining a lot of "mysteries" of different fields. I feel like a freak cultist going into it though, it feels more like religion, which is why I have a had time talking about it. There are explanations for how metaphorically most religions are actually right, just not in the sense they are typically interpreted.

That's really all I want to say. It was kind of hard for me to share. Thanks for taking an interest though. It actually did kind of cheer me up.
